# Local acceptance

**This file is retained as the historical (pre-Milestone-1) narrative record.** As of Milestone 1, the machine-readable gate is no longer hand-authored: it is generated by [`ENV2_COMPOSE/scripts/local-acceptance.py`](../../ENV2_COMPOSE/scripts/local-acceptance.py) directly from named run artifacts, written to `local-acceptance.json` (schema 2) with a generated human-readable summary at [LOCAL_ACCEPTANCE_GENERATED.md](LOCAL_ACCEPTANCE_GENERATED.md). Schema 2 separates what this document's table below conflates into a single row: **`route_fidelity`** is the freeze requirement (every in-scope route/profile's ending state matches either the normal expected state or a source-predicted failure declared in `TWIN_SPEC/expected-failures.yaml`), and **`product_route_health`** is informational only (did the business route actually complete -- Shared Kafka is `false` here by design, with its expected-failure citation, and this is the number a later red-agent judge consumes). For the current gate and its evidence, read `LOCAL_ACCEPTANCE_GENERATED.md`, not the table below.

## Interpretation

The original 26 checks exercise explicitly selected synthetic states and several direct dependency callbacks/faults; they are not a claim that every production route or concurrency schedule is equivalent. The six additional route cases exercise real bank outcomes and manual return reconciliation; the six bank cases include bounded nonterminal observations. [ROUTE_COVERAGE.md](ROUTE_COVERAGE.md) separates transport evidence from fixture labels and distinguishes terminal success from expected held state.

The replay comparator validates JUnit and complete traces before comparing. It normalizes only documented generated identities, exact clock fields, generated bank UTRs and unordered capture collections; monetary values, statuses, unknown payload fields, mutations and duplicate multiplicity remain material. A passing comparison establishes equality of those recorded observations, not byte-identical databases or every unobserved intermediate scheduling state.

Real Docker negative tests for command timeout and SIGTERM intentionally return failed audit status and verify cleanup. They are separate lifecycle evidence, not passing network-invariant workloads: [timeout](runs/audit-timeout-negative/cleanup-verification.json), [interrupt](runs/audit-interrupt-negative/cleanup-verification.json).

The full implementation and exact run/cleanup commands are in [TWIN_V1_README.md](../../TWIN_V1_README.md). Remote gates require explicit company transfer approval, passed local acceptance and a hash-bound execution plan; none is bypassed by setting an environment variable alone.
